entries.title: Choose a federation: tested or untested sets who you lift against
entries.take: Tested federations drug test lifters; untested ones do not. The federation also sets your rules, classes and gear list.
entries.body: USA Powerlifting limits competition to members who have not used performance-enhancing drugs for 36 months before the meet, and members can be tested at any time. The USPA offers tested meets only with national office approval, labels them 'Tested' and keeps their results separate from untested meets. IPF coaches in the warm-up and lifting area must acknowledge the IPF Anti-Doping Rules. Classes and gear lists differ, so read the rulebook of the federation you enter.
do: Find the federation's meet calendar and read its current rulebook before you enter.

entries.title: Register, then pick a class you can reach by normal eating
entries.take: Join the federation, enter the meet by its deadline and choose a class near your normal weight.
entries.body: USA Powerlifting memberships run from January 1 to December 31. USPA membership covers 12 months from the date of issue. Meets set their own entry forms, fees and deadlines. USPA requires ID and your membership card at weigh-in, and IPF weigh-in requires ID or a passport. Class limits differ between federations (see the class table), so check the one used by your meet.
do: Read the meet's entry form for deadlines, fees and the weigh-in schedule.
Choose the class you can hold with normal eating, not a cut.

entries.title: Buy legal gear early and train in it
entries.take: In IPF rules you need a singlet, a T-shirt under it, shoes and shin-length socks for the deadlift; belt, sleeves and wraps are optional.
entries.body: IPF limits: belt up to 10 cm (3.9 in) wide and 13 mm (0.5 in) thick; knee sleeves up to 7 mm thick and 30 cm (11.8 in) long; wrist wraps up to 1 m (39 in) long and 8 cm (3.1 in) wide; shoe soles up to 5 cm (2 in). Hats are not allowed. Belts, singlets and sleeves must come from makers on the IPF Approved List. USA Powerlifting uses the same sleeve and wrist wrap limits. Wear all of it in the last heavy sessions.
do: Check each item against your federation's approved list before you buy it.
Wear the full kit for your last heavy sessions.

entries.title: Plan nine attempts with your coach or a trusted friend
entries.take: Plan an opener you could lift easily on any day, a realistic second, and a hard but makeable third.
entries.body: Elite classic lifters at IPF World Championships opened near 91% of their expected third attempt, then added about 5% for the second and about 3% for the third. Base your plan on your best recent single, not on a hope. Write all nine weights down with a lighter plan B for each lift, and round to 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) steps.
do: Use the attempt table below, and your best recent single, to fill in all nine weights.

entries.title: Taper over the last week or two: less volume, a few heavy singles
entries.take: Survey data show a step taper with 41-50% less volume, the last heavy squat and deadlift 7-10 days out, and rest in the last days.
entries.body: In 364 North American raw powerlifters, a step taper over 7 to 10 days with 41-50% less volume was typical. The last heavy squat and deadlift came 7 to 10 days out, the last heavy bench under 7 days out, and full rest about 2.8 days before the meet. In a small trial of 19 athletes, 3 days off kept upper- and lower-body strength; 5 days off cost upper-body strength.
do: Keep the lifts, cut the sets, and stop hard training about 3 days out.

entries.title: Confirm the schedule, travel and food for the meet
entries.take: Know your session, weigh-in time and flight, and have travel and meals sorted before the last days.
entries.body: Find your session and flight on the meet schedule and confirm with the meet director. Book a bed close to the venue if the drive is long. Plan your food for the day before and the day of the meet, and pack the bag early. Squat and bench rack heights are written down at weigh-in, so measure yours in training.
do: Pack the bag a few days early using the checklist below.
Note your squat and bench rack heights and foot-block settings.

entries.title: Lay out gear, eat familiar food and sleep as normally as you can
entries.take: Eat meals that you know sit well, drink fluids steadily and avoid new foods or heavy training.
entries.body: Lay out singlet, T-shirt, socks, belt, shoes and ID. Skip new foods and alcohol. A poor night before a meet is common and a single night with little sleep had little effect on muscle strength in a systematic review of 17 studies, while several nights of restricted sleep could reduce force in compound lifts. Go to bed at your usual time and do not worry about one bad night.
do: Keep the day light: a short walk and easy mobility at most.
Go to bed at your normal time.

entries.title: Weigh in about two hours before lifting, with ID and your opening attempts
entries.take: IPF and USA Powerlifting weigh-ins run for 90 minutes and start two hours before lifting; the USPA can offer one up to 24 hours before.
entries.body: IPF: weigh-in no earlier than two hours before the start for a category and lasts one and a half hours; bring ID or a passport; opening attempts are declared at weigh-in. USA Powerlifting: weigh-in starts two hours before lifting, lasts 90 minutes and ends 30 minutes before lifting. USPA: weigh-in lasts at least 90 minutes, with an optional early weigh-in up to 24 hours before lifting. If you miss class weight, you may return to the scale within the window.
do: Arrive early, bring ID and your written openers, and keep your gear bag with you.

entries.title: Pass the equipment check and sign the rack height sheet
entries.take: Referees inspect and approve each item you plan to wear; an illegal item found later can disqualify you.
entries.body: IPF: at least two referees inspect gear any time up to 30 minutes before your category starts; unclean or torn items are rejected, and over-length wraps can be cut and resubmitted. If you appear on the platform with an illegal item, you are disqualified. USA Powerlifting: every competitor has an equipment check, normally during the weigh-in period, with a 30-minute deadline before the session. Check squat and bench rack heights and sign the sheet.
do: Bring every item you plan to wear, including your belt and sleeves.
Sign the rack height sheet after checking each height.

entries.title: Eat and drink steadily after weigh-in, using food you know
entries.take: After weigh-in, eat a familiar meal and sip fluids, then keep snacks nearby for the rest of the day.
entries.body: Eat normal, familiar foods and avoid very large or high-fibre meals just before the first squat. A systematic review of 49 carbohydrate studies found extra carbohydrate did not improve acute performance in 13 studies, and helped in six, mainly in fasted lifters or workouts of more than 10 sets per muscle group. A meet day is long, so steady eating and drinking matters more than any single food.
do: Eat a normal meal within an hour of weigh-in.
Sip fluids across the morning instead of drinking a large amount at once.

entries.title: Time your warm-up from the flight order, not the clock
entries.take: Work backwards from your opener: count the lifters ahead of you and finish your last warm-up a few lifters before your call.
entries.body: Check the board for the flight order and watch how fast the platform moves. A common plan is a general warm-up, then 4 to 6 ramping sets on the bar, with the last warm-up about three to four lifters before your opener. Under IPF rules a single group gets 20 minutes between lifts, and each lifter has one minute to start after being called. Ask a coach or loader if you are unsure how many lifters are left.
do: Ask the warm-up room staff how many lifters are ahead of you every few minutes.
Be ready at the platform area when the lifter before you takes the bar.

entries.title: Squat: wait for the command, reach depth, wait for 'rack'
entries.take: After unracking, stand still with knees locked and wait for 'Squat'; squat below parallel, stand up, then wait for 'Rack'.
entries.body: IPF: step back, stand motionless with knees locked, and wait for the downward arm movement and 'Squat'. The top of the legs at the hip joint must go lower than the top of the knees, in one descent, then you rise with knees locked and wait for 'Rack'. If you are not in position after five seconds you hear 'Replace'. USA Powerlifting and the USPA use the same words. Foot movement, double bounces and missing a command can turn the lift down.
do: Settle, take a breath and wait for the full command before you move.

entries.title: Bench: wait for 'start', pause on the chest, wait for 'press'
entries.take: Lock the elbows and wait for 'Start'; lower the bar to your chest, hold still, wait for 'Press', then press and wait for 'Rack'.
entries.body: IPF: head, shoulders and buttocks stay on the bench and feet stay flat on the floor. Grip with thumbs around the bar and hands no wider than 81 cm (32 in) between the forefingers. After 'Start', the bar goes to the chest or abdominal area and the underside of the elbows reaches level with or below the shoulders. Hold motionless until 'Press', then lock the arms and wait for 'Rack'. USA Powerlifting and the USPA use the same words.
do: Practise the pause on every training rep, with a count you can repeat.

entries.title: Deadlift: pull to a full lockout and wait for 'down'
entries.take: Stand erect with knees locked and shoulders back and wait for 'Down'; then lower the bar with control.
entries.body: IPF, USA Powerlifting and USPA use one command, 'Down', given once the bar is held motionless at a full lockout. Reasons for a turn-down include downward movement of the bar before lockout, supporting the bar on the thighs, lowering it before the command, losing control with both hands, and stepping. Foot movement after the command is not a fault. In IPF and USA Powerlifting meets you may change a third-attempt deadlift twice, unless you were already called to a bar loaded to your submitted weight.
do: Stand tall, hold the lockout for a beat, and wait for the command.

entries.title: Between flights: small snacks, fluids, and caffeine only if tried
entries.take: Eat and drink in small amounts between lifts and try any caffeine in training first.
entries.body: A meta-analysis of 10 strength studies found caffeine gave a small strength gain overall (standardised mean difference 0.20, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.36), clearer for the upper body than the lower body. Keep snacks small and familiar, and keep fluid steady. Caffeine affects people differently, so use only what you have used in training and stop if it causes jitters or an upset stomach.
do: Eat a small familiar snack and sip fluid after each discipline.
Use caffeine only in amounts you have tried in training.

entries.title: After the meet: results, food, rest and a review
entries.take: Collect your results, eat and rest, and review what the attempts taught you before you plan the next cycle.
entries.body: Ask for the score sheet and any video, and note which attempts were turned down and the reason shown on the cards. Eat and drink normally and take a few easy days before hard training starts. In tested federations you can be asked for a sample after lifting; follow the doping control officer's instructions. Write down what you would change about openers, warm-ups and food for the next meet.
do: Write a short review the next day, while details are fresh.

entries.title: Classes, gear lists and drug testing differ between federations
entries.take: IPF has 8 classes per sex; USA Powerlifting and the USPA list 12 each; check the one you will enter.
entries.body: IPF men's classes run from 59 kg to 120+ kg and women's from 47 kg to 84+ kg, plus a lowest sub-junior and junior class of 53 kg (men) or 43 kg (women). USA Powerlifting has 12 classes per sex (men 52 to 140+ kg, women 44 to 100+ kg). The USPA lists 12 (men 52 to 140.1+ kg, women 44 to 110+ kg). Gear must meet the federation's lists, and testing rules differ.
do: Check the class table, then the rulebook, of the federation that runs your meet.

entries.title: Three referees show white or red lights, then cards give the reason
entries.take: White means good lift and red means no lift; after the lights come up, cards show why a lift was turned down.
entries.body: In IPF rules each referee controls a white and a red light, and the lights come on together. A red, blue or yellow card (1, 2, 3) shows the reason for a failure. Common reasons: squat depth, double bounce or not standing erect, stepping and missed commands. Bench: bar not reaching the chest or elbows not low enough, downward movement or no lockout, heaving and missed commands. Deadlift: knees or shoulders not locked, supporting the bar on the thighs, lowering early or losing control.
do: Ask your coach to note the card colours so you can fix the cause.

entries.title: You can change an opener once; second attempts and bench or squat thirds are locked
entries.take: You submit each next weight within one minute of the lights; after that, changes are tightly limited.
entries.body: IPF: one change on the first attempt of each lift, higher or lower, up to three minutes before the first round starts for the first group. Second attempts and third attempts in squat and bench cannot be changed. In the third deadlift round you may change twice unless the bar has been called loaded. Weights are multiples of 2.5 kg (5.5 lb) with at least 2.5 kg between attempts. If you miss, you do not follow yourself; the next attempt comes in the next round. USA Powerlifting uses the same structure.
do: Give your coach the written plan, the minimum increment, and who submits the card.

entries.title: Caffeine gave a small strength gain in upper-body lifts
entries.take: A meta-analysis of 10 strength studies found a small gain overall, clearer for upper-body strength.
entries.body: Caffeine improved strength (standardised mean difference 0.20, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.36) and power. For upper-body strength the effect was 0.21 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.39); for lower-body strength it was 0.15 (95% CI -0.05 to 0.34), not clearly different from zero. Effects differ between people and the evidence in women is thin. Avoid trying it for the first time at a meet.
do: Try your planned dose in training before the meet.

entries.title: Aim for nine good lifts and a smooth day, not a personal record
entries.take: A first meet is practice for the whole day: weigh-in, warm-ups, commands and timing.
entries.body: Choose an opener that you could lift easily, take a realistic second and add a third only if the second felt solid. Good first-meet goals are hitting all commands, making nine good lifts and learning the flow of a meet. Records and totals come later. Bring a coach or friend who can read the flight order and keep the attempt plan.
do: Set two process goals, such as clean commands and on-time warm-ups.

entries.title: Tested meets use drug testing; untested meets may not
entries.take: A federation or meet name tells you which one it is; tested and untested results are kept separate.
entries.body: USA Powerlifting competes members who have not used performance-enhancing drugs for 36 months and can test members at any time. The USPA allows meet directors to run tested meets with approval, labels them 'Tested' and keeps results and records separate from untested meets. Which one you choose changes who you compete against and whether records count. This is not advice on medicines; ask a doctor if you take any prescription.
do: Check whether a meet is tested before you register.

entries.title: Opening with a weight that is nearly a max
entries.take: An opener that is hard to lift risks all three attempts and a total; keep it around 88-92% of a current best single.
entries.body: Elite classic lifters opened near 91% of their expected third attempt. A heavy opener burns nerves and energy, and a miss uses one of three tries. First-time lifters often over-pick because the day feels exciting. Pick a weight you could lift for a clean double on a normal day, then build.
do: Choose an opener from your best recent single, then drop it a little if unsure.

entries.title: Arriving with gear you never checked against the rulebook
entries.take: Gear that is not on the list, is too long or too thick, or is torn gets rejected at the equipment check.
entries.body: IPF inspectors reject unclean or torn items and gear outside the stated limits, such as a belt over 10 cm (3.9 in) wide or sleeves over 7 mm thick. An item found illegal on the platform after inspection can lead to disqualification. USA Powerlifting requires an equipment check for every competitor. Hats are not allowed on the platform in IPF rules.
do: Compare every item with the rulebook two weeks before the meet.

entries.title: Missing your call because the warm-up ran long
entries.take: You have one minute to start your attempt after the bar is called ready; a late start forfeits it.
entries.body: IPF: the lifter has one minute from the speaker's call to start the attempt, or the attempt is forfeited. Warm-ups that start too early leave you cold and bored; too late and you walk to the platform rushed. Count lifters ahead of you, use the board, and ask staff when unsure.
do: Finish the last warm-up several lifters before your opener.
Check rack height before you are called.

entries.title: Trying new food or a big meal after weigh-in
entries.take: A large or unfamiliar meal after weigh-in can leave you full or ill when the first squat comes.
entries.body: Familiar food is the safe choice. A review of 49 carbohydrate studies found no clear acute strength gain from extra carbohydrate in most cases, so there is little reason to experiment on the day. Eat what has worked on a heavy training day, and keep portions moderate.
do: Rehearse your meet-day meals on a heavy training day.

entries.title: Opener as a share of your current best single
entries.take: A conservative first attempt; elite classic lifters opened near 91% of their expected third attempt.

entries.title: Second attempt as a share of your current best single
entries.take: A step up from the opener of about 5% for elite classic lifters; a realistic, solid weight.

entries.title: Third attempt as a share of your current best single
entries.take: An aim around your best single, up to a small personal best if the day feels good.

entries.title: Weigh-in start before lifting
entries.take: IPF: no earlier than two hours before the category starts. USA Powerlifting: weigh-in starts two hours before lifting.

entries.title: Length of the weigh-in period
entries.take: IPF: one and a half hours. USA Powerlifting: 90 minutes, ending 30 minutes before lifting. USPA: at least 90 minutes.

entries.title: Time to start an attempt after being called
entries.take: IPF: one minute from the speaker's call to the start of the attempt; USPA also gives one minute.

entries.title: Minimum step between attempts
entries.take: IPF weights are multiples of 2.5 kg, with at least 2.5 kg between attempts. USA Powerlifting uses 2.5 kg increments.

entries.title: Time to leave the platform after an attempt
entries.take: IPF and USA Powerlifting: leave the platform within 30 seconds of the end of an attempt.

entries.title: Opener (first attempt)
entries.take: The first of your three attempts on a lift; chosen to be easy enough that you lift it with room to spare.

entries.title: Flight (group)
entries.take: A group of lifters who take their attempts together; larger sessions split into flights, with lower previous totals lifting first in IPF rules.

entries.title: Lot number
entries.take: A number drawn at weigh-in; if two lifters choose the same weight, the lower lot number lifts first.

entries.title: Classic (raw)
entries.take: A division with a non-supportive singlet and no supportive suits, shirts or knee wraps; belt, knee sleeves and wrist wraps are allowed within limits.

entries.title: Chief referee
entries.take: The referee who gives the commands on the platform; two side referees also judge each lift.

entries.title: Spotter/loaders
entries.take: Helpers who load the bar and spot squat and bench; two to five are on the platform at a time in IPF rules.

entries.title: Rack height sheet
entries.take: The form where you record squat and bench rack and foot-block settings at weigh-in, so loaders set them before your attempt.

entries.title: Bomb out
entries.take: To miss all three attempts on a lift; in a full-power meet that usually means no total.

entries.title: IPF weight classes for men and women, in kg and lb
entries.take: IPF classes from the 2026 Technical Rules Book; pounds are converted from the kilogram limits.
rows: Sub-junior and junior only: up to 53.0 kg
Sub-junior and junior only: up to 43.0 kg

entries.title: Platform commands for each lift
entries.take: Commands as given by the chief referee in IPF, USA Powerlifting and USPA rules; wait for each one.
rows: Depth: top of legs at the hip below the top of the knees
Arms locked and still for 'Start'; bar still on chest for 'Press'
Elbows level with or below the shoulders at the chest
Stand erect, knees locked, shoulders back
One command, given once the lockout is held
Fix the reason the referee gives you
IPF: if not in position after five seconds

entries.title: Attempt selection ranges for a first meet
entries.take: Typical ranges as a share of a current best single, with an example for a lifter whose best single is 200 kg (441 lb).
rows: A weight you could lift easily on any day

entries.title: Meet bag checklist
entries.take: Pack in the days before the meet, and check the rules of your federation for each item.

groups.name: Required to lift
items: Singlet
T-shirt to wear under the singlet
Shin-length socks for the deadlift
Lifting shoes or deadlift slippers
Photo ID or passport
Federation membership card

groups.name: Optional gear (if your federation allows)
items: Belt (IPF: up to 10 cm / 3.9 in wide, 13 mm thick)
Knee sleeves (up to 7 mm thick, 30 cm / 11.8 in long)
Wrist wraps (up to 1 m / 39 in long, 8 cm / 3.1 in wide)
Chalk or baby powder, if the meet allows it
Medical tape for thumbs (IPF: two layers at most)

groups.name: Paperwork and plan
items: Entry confirmation and the meet schedule
Written plan for all nine attempts
Squat and bench rack heights and foot-block settings
Pen and notebook

groups.name: Food and drink
items: Familiar meal for after weigh-in
Small snacks for between flights
Water or a drink you have used in training
Caffeine only if you have tried it in training

groups.name: Comfort and recovery
items: Spare T-shirt and socks
Towel
Warm layer for the warm-up room
Phone charger
A friend or coach to hand up attempt cards

ipf-2026.title: IPF Technical Rules Book 2026 (effective 1 March 2026, v3)
ipf-2026.support: Weighing in ... no earlier than two hours before the start of the competition ... The weigh in period will last one and a half hours. Squat/Bench/Deadlift rules of performance 4.1-4.3 (commands 'Squat', 'Rack', 'Start', 'Press', 'Down'); 2.8 lights; 2.9 failure cards; 3.12 inspection; 6.1 round system.

usapl-2026.title: USA Powerlifting Rulebook, version 2026.2
usapl-2026.edition: Version 2026.2, updated 9 February 2026, in effect 1 January 2026
usapl-2026.support: 5.1.1 Weighing in of competitors must begin two (2) hours before the scheduled start of lifting for a given session and must last 90 minutes. There must be 30 minutes between the end of the weigh-in period and the start of lifting. 1.8 weight classes. 5.5.2 Competition is limited to members who have not used any form of performance enhancing drugs for 36 months.

uspa-2025.title: USPA Technical Rules 2025v1
uspa-2025.edition: 2025v1, dated 24 March 2025 (the file linked from uspa.net/rulebook)
uspa-2025.support: 1.3.1 weight classes; 1.8.1-1.8.2 tested meets optional and labelled 'Tested'; 5.1.2 An optional early weigh in session ... up to, but not greater than 24 hours prior to the start of the lifting session; 5.1.3 weigh in sessions will last a minimum of one and a half hours.

travis-attempts-2021.title: Weight Selection Attempts of Elite Classic Powerlifters
travis-attempts-2021.support: Male (n = 66) and female (n = 43) powerlifters who completed all lifts successfully at an IPF Classic World Championship between 2012-2019 ... selecting an opener of ~91% of the expected A3 weight, followed by ~5% increase from A1 to A2, and ~3% increase from A2 to A3 represent the typical weight selection attempts ...

travis-2021.title: Characterizing the Tapering Practices of United States and Canadian Raw Powerlifters
travis-2021.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
travis-2021.support: A total of 364 powerlifters completed a 41-item survey. A step taper was primarily used over 7-10 days while decreasing the training volume by 41-50% ... The final heavy back squat and deadlift sessions were completed 7-10 days before competition, whereas the final heavy bench press session was completed <7 days before competition ... Complete training cessation was implemented 2.8 +/- 1.1 days before competition.

travis-2022.title: The Effects of 3 vs. 5 Days of Training Cessation on Maximal Strength
travis-2022.support: Nineteen strength-trained athletes ... maximal lower-body strength can be preserved during 3 and 5 days of training cessation, but maximal upper-body strength is only preserved for 3 days.

grgic-2017.title: Tapering Practices of Croatian Open-Class Powerlifting Champions
grgic-2017.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
grgic-2017.support: Ten Croatian open-class powerlifting champions ... the same equipment was used as during competition.

grgic-2018.title: Effects of caffeine intake on muscle strength and power: a systematic review and meta-analysis
grgic-2018.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
grgic-2018.support: Ten studies on the strength outcome ... Caffeine ingestion improved both strength (SMD = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.03, 0.36; p = 0.023) and power ... improves upper (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI: 0.02, 0.39) but not lower body strength (SMD = 0.15; 95% CI: -0.05, 0.34).

henselmans-2022.title: The Effect of Carbohydrate Intake on Strength and Resistance Training Performance: A Systematic Review
henselmans-2022.support: Forty-nine studies were included: 19 acute, six glycogen depletion, seven short-term and 17 long-term studies. Acutely, higher carbohydrate intake did not improve performance in 13 studies and enhanced performance in six studies, primarily in those with fasted control groups and workouts with over 10 sets per muscle group.

knowles-2018.title: Inadequate sleep and muscle strength: Implications for resistance training
knowles-2018.journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
knowles-2018.support: Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria ... Sleep deprivation had little effect on muscle strength during resistance exercise. In contrast, consecutive nights of sleep restriction could reduce the force output of multi-joint, but not single-joint movements.
